ladder.teaches: converging pointers on a sorted array (pair sum)
ladder.why: The canonical first rung: on a sorted array, a sum that is too small can only be fixed by moving the left pointer, too big only by moving the right one.

ladder.teaches: compare from both ends (palindromes)

ladder.teaches: walk two sequences together (merge)
ladder.why: The two ends of a sorted array with negatives are two sorted sequences of squares; comparing the ends and writing from the back is an O(n) merge.

ladder.teaches: converging pointers on a sorted array (pair sum)

ladder.teaches: compare from both ends (palindromes)
ladder.why: Mirror-pair comparison applied block by block, where each mismatched pair costs exactly one change.

ladder.teaches: compare from both ends (palindromes)

ladder.teaches: fix one element, two-pointer the rest, skip duplicates (3Sum)

ladder.teaches: move the side that cannot improve (container)
ladder.why: The side with the smaller running max already knows its water level, so settle it and move it: the container argument with an insight.

ladder.teaches: greedy with a counter or a heap of the best so far

ladder.teaches: greedy with a counter or a heap of the best so far

ladder.teaches: variable window: the longest valid (shrink while invalid)
